groups.title: Eye Drops (D64600COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for discomfort while wearing soft or hard contact lenses, for supplementing tears (dryness of the eye), for eye fatigue and for blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 2 to 3 drops per dose, 5 to 6 times in 1 day. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container immediately (single-use products only).
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have ever had an allergic reaction to a medicine, if you have an allergic constitution, if you have glaucoma, or if you have severe eye pain.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not use it if the solution is cloudy. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. At first use, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not share it with other people. For a single-use product, use it only once after opening and discard the remaining solution and the container immediately.

If rash, reddening (flushing of the skin), itching, redness of the eye, itching or swelling of the eye occurs, or if a wearer of hard contact lenses has a lot of discharge such as eye mucus or the lenses become cloudy, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Discomfort with contact lenses, tear supplementation (dry eye), eye fatigue and blurred eyes

groups.title: Tablet (118601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 14 years and older: take 1 to 2 tablets (8 to 16 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Children aged 6 years to under 14 years: take 1/2 to 1 tablet (4 to 8 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. Children aged 2 years to under 6 years: take 1/2 tablet (4 mg) per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you are breast-feeding, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have gastric ulcer, severe kidney impairment, hepatic failure or severe liver disease, impaired bronchial motility with copious secretions, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are an older person.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, cefuroxime, amoxicillin, doxycycline or oxytetracycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: severe skin disorders such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); non-specific influenza-like symptoms (fever, body aches, rhinitis, cough and sore throat); diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain; occasionally headache, rash, difficulty breathing, transient chills; or hypersensitivity reactions such as urticaria, bronchospasm, angioedema, itching or signs of anaphylactic shock.

summaryTable.What it is for: Difficulty bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis

groups.title: Syrup (123841ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum (phlegm) in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, bronchiectasis and pharyngitis, for drainage of pus in chronic sinusitis, and for drainage in exudative otitis media (middle ear inflammation).
groups.usage: Adults: initially take 15 mL (750 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day; when symptoms improve, take 10 mL (500 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 13 years to 18 years: take 5 mL to 10 mL (250 to 500 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Ages 6 years to 12 years: take 5 mL (250 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages 2 years to 5 years: take 5 mL to 10 mL (250 to 500 mg) in 1 day, divided into 4 doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if you are an older person, if you have liver impairment or heart impairment, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to caramel.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an antibiotic or with a syrup containing trimetoquinol hydrochloride.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely nausea, vomiting, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, gastrointestinal bleeding or heartburn; occasionally loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, thirst; in sensitive people stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), rash, erythema (red patches) or eczema; rarely headache; in sensitive people rhinitis; occasionally itching, palpitations, runny nose, a feeling of pressure over the whole body; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), liver function disorder with raised AST, ALT, ALP or LDH, jaundice, or shock.

summaryTable.What it is for: Difficulty bringing up sputum in bronchitis, bronchial asthma, bronchiectasis and pharyngitis; drainage in chronic sinusitis and exudative otitis media

groups.title: Tablet (104601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the improvement of symptoms that accompany abnormal vitamin D metabolism in chronic renal failure, hypoparathyroidism and vitamin D-resistant rickets and osteomalacia (hypocalcaemia, tetany, bone pain, bone lesions and the like), and for osteoporosis.
groups.usage: For chronic renal failure and osteoporosis in adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (0.5 to 1 microgram) by mouth, 1 time in 1 day. For hypoparathyroidism and other diseases caused by abnormal vitamin D metabolism in adults: take 2 to 8 tablets (1 to 4 micrograms) by mouth, 1 time in 1 day. For osteoporosis in children: take 0.01 to 0.03 micrograms per kg of body weight by mouth, 1 time in 1 day. For other diseases in children: take 0.05 to 0.1 micrograms per kg of body weight by mouth, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, hypercalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hypermagnesaemia, a Ca x P product greater than 3.7 (mmol/L)2, alkalaemia with a blood pH above 7.44 (milk-alkali syndrome, Burnett's syndrome), or signs of vitamin D toxicity.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a child or an older person, if you have a history of kidney stones, or if you have sarcoidosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Follow the instructions you have been given about calcium intake from the diet or from supplements.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take magnesium-containing preparations, vitamin D and its derivatives, calcium-containing preparations or thiazide diuretics. Consult a pharmacist if you are taking digitalis, a resin such as cholestyramine, the laxative mineral oil, phenytoin, glucocorticoids, colestipol, sucralfate, an antacid with a high aluminium content, oestrogens (ethinylestradiol, norethisterone), barbiturates or antiepileptic medicines.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: occasionally gastrointestinal disorders such as loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation or stomach pain, stomach discomfort, abdominal distension, indigestion; rarely thirst or an abnormal sensation in the mouth; excessive drinking and thirst, pancreatitis, a metallic taste, cramp of the leg muscles, headache, a heavy head, insomnia, irritability, weakness, lassitude, dizziness, numbness, drowsiness, heartburn, stiff shoulder, senile hearing loss, tinnitus (ringing in the ears), decline of memory and recall, overt psychosis, other disturbance of consciousness, back pain, a mild rise in blood pressure; rarely palpitations, other cardiac arrhythmia, acute renal failure, raised BUN and creatinine (reduced kidney function), kidney stones, other nephrocalcinosis, liver function disorder, jaundice, itching, rash, a feeling of heat, conjunctival congestion, other conjunctivitis, corneal calcification, sensitivity to light, calcification around the joints (bone formation), other bone pain, hoarseness, oedema (swelling), other weight loss, difficulty passing urine, polyuria (excessive urine), night-time urination, ectopic calcification, muscle pain, runny nose, high fever, reduced libido, protein in the urine or high blood cholesterol.

summaryTable.What it is for: Symptoms of abnormal vitamin D metabolism in chronic renal failure, hypoparathyroidism and vitamin D-resistant rickets and osteomalacia, and osteoporosis

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E12700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is an infant aged 3 months or older and under 2 years, or a young child; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Consult a pharmacist if you are taking a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes); cough with breathlessness and difficulty breathing; fever; or signs of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like).

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Troche (A00401ATO)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammation caused by pharyngitis, tonsillitis and stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth).
groups.usage: Adults: let 1 tablet (1.5 mg) dissolve slowly in the mouth 4 to 5 times in 1 day, without chewing it and without swallowing it. The amount may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine in infants and young children aged 3 years or younger.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have allergic contact eczema, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Do not chew it and do not swallow it; let it dissolve slowly in the saliva and keep it in the mouth as long as possible so that it stays in the mouth for a long time.

If rash or a hypersensitivity reaction of the oral mucosa (urticaria, erosion, and rarely a burning sensation in the mouth and throat) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist. High fever, headache and nausea may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of inflammation caused by pharyngitis, tonsillitis and stomatitis

groups.title: Capsule (379302ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (40 mg as iron) per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day, avoiding mealtimes.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis, impaired iron utilisation, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, anaemia due to bone marrow failure, haemolytic anaemia, iron overload, pernicious anaemia, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis or liver cirrhosis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis, impaired heart or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. For the best effect it is better to take it apart from meals.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking an iron-containing preparation (an iron supplement, an MRI liver contrast agent and the like), an anti-aldosterone medicine, triamterene, a quinolone, penicillamine, neomycin, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, vitamin E, a diphosphonate salt, thyroxine, a cefdinir preparation, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: urticaria, itching, skin hypersensitivity on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, coma; occasionally raised AST and ALT; rarely raised ALP; nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, tooth discoloration or stomach discomfort.

summaryTable.What it is for: Iron deficiency anaemia

groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet (80 mg as iron) per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day, after meals, swallowing it without chewing.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis, impaired iron utilisation, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, anaemia due to bone marrow failure, chronic haemolytic anaemia, iron overload, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis or liver cirrhosis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis, impaired heart or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney impairment, hypoproteinaemia, delayed gastric emptying, pyloric stenosis or a gastrointestinal diverticulum, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an iron-containing preparation (an iron supplement, an MRI liver contrast agent and the like), an anti-aldosterone medicine, triamterene, a diphosphonate salt, thyroxine, a cefdinir preparation, salicylic acid, phenylbutazone, oxyphenbutazone, a quinolone, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, a preparation such as vitamin E, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: urticaria, itching, skin hypersensitivity on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, coma; occasionally raised AST and ALT; rarely raised ALP; nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, tooth discoloration or stomach discomfort.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E30500ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, up to a limit of 2 times in 1 day, preferably on an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. For the first dose, take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool. Do not use it continuously for more than 1 week.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), a history of hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil, or hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Unless it is really necessary, it is better for children aged 10 years or younger to avoid taking it. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an intravenous lipid preparation.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (C89900ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 sachet per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Take only the smallest stated amount, with an interval of at least 4 hours. Dissolve 1 sachet in about 250 mL of hot water that is not boiling and drink it within 10 to 15 minutes.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma caused by another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor or have taken one within the past 2 weeks; if you have high blood pressure, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe reduction of heart function, epilepsy, aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic) now or in the past, or diabetes; if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol; if the user is under 18 years of age; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you are breast-feeding; if you have a hereditary problem such as glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, sucrase deficiency, fructose intolerance or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you have phenylketonuria and must restrict phenylalanine intake, because this medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised to phenylalanine; if you have respiratory failure or a risk of it (for example chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pneumonia or asthma); or if you have phaeochromocytoma.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a constitution prone to allergy, obstructive vascular disease (Raynaud's syndrome), liver impairment, kidney impairment, a history of peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a tendency to bleed (abnormal platelet function), impaired heart function, emphysema, asthma or chronic bronchitis, thyroid disease, difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia, glaucoma or closed-angle glaucoma, a history of pre-eclampsia; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have hypersensitivity to Red No. 40.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness, dizziness, reduced vision and impairment of cognition and psychomotor function may occur, so avoid driving and operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, antihistamines, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, other sympathomimetic medicines (decongestants, appetite suppressants, amphetamines and the like), antihypertensive medicines (vasodilators, beta blockers, debrisoquine, guanethidine, reserpine, methyldopa and the like), metoclopramide, domperidone, cholestyramine, warfarin, coumarin anticoagulants, chloramphenicol, zidovudine, probenecid, digoxin and other cardiac glycosides, ergot alkaloids (ergotamine, methysergide), amiodarone, haloperidol or quinidine.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: a severe sore throat, or a sore throat lasting 2 days or more with fever, headache, rash, nausea or vomiting; fever lasting 3 days or more; cough or nasal congestion lasting 7 days or more; very rarely signs of shock (anaphylactoid symptoms: difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity reactions (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), raised blood pressure, reflex bradycardia, tachycardia, dizziness, drowsiness, nervousness, insomnia, sedation, lassitude, persistent headache, convulsions, abnormal sensation, dyskinesia, muscle cramps, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite; with long-term use gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation; rash, allergic reactions, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), raised AST, raised ALT, or fixed drug eruption.

groups.title: Patch (A88115CPC)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid when stopping smoking.
groups.usage: Adults: apply 1 patch 1 time in 1 day to a hairless part of the body (the buttock, the inner arm and the like), changing the site of application every day. Nicotinell TTS 30 is generally used for smokers of 20 or more cigarettes a day, and Nicotinell TTS 20 for smokers of up to 20 cigarettes a day. Nicotinell TTS 10 is used in the final stage to reduce nicotine replacement. A heavy smoker starts with Nicotinell TTS 30, then Nicotinell TTS 20, and finally Nicotinell TTS 10, each for 4 weeks. An ordinary smoker uses Nicotinell TTS 20 for 8 weeks and then Nicotinell TTS 10 for 4 weeks. Treatment must not exceed 3 months.
groups.caution:
If you continue to smoke while using this medicine, cardiovascular adverse effects of nicotine may occur more often and more markedly, so it should be used only by people who have stopped smoking completely.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; a chronic skin disease (psoriasis, chronic dermatitis, urticaria); a generalised skin disease; hypersensitivity dermatitis; unstable angina or worsening angina; myocardial infarction within the past 3 months; the late phase after an acute infarction; severe cardiac arrhythmia; systemic hypertension; peripheral vascular disease; cerebrovascular disease (acute stroke, cerebrovascular abnormality); if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if the user is a child or adolescent under 18 years of age; or if the user is a non-smoker or an occasional smoker.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have gastritis, peptic ulcer, occlusive arterial disease, stable angina, heart failure, decompensated heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, vasospasm, uncontrolled high blood pressure, an arterial bypass graft or angioplasty, kidney failure, liver failure, diabetes, hyperthyroidism or phaeochromocytoma.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, oestrogens, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (prazosin, labetalol and the like), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (isoprenaline, phenylephrine), propoxyphene, the diuretic furosemide, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, theophylline, tacrine, clozapine or ropinirole.

If any of the following occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: erythema (red patches), a burning sensation, blisters, skin rash or tightness at the site of application; agitation, anxiety, nervousness, insomnia, abnormal dreams, headache, dizziness, dyskinesia, disturbance of attention, somnolence (drowsiness), emotional instability, irritability, depression, confusion, tremor; palpitations, high blood pressure, flushing, chest pain, difficulty breathing, arrhythmia, cough, upper respiratory tract infection; nausea, abdominal pain, indigestion, vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, abdominal distension, dry mouth; skin reactions at the site of application, excessive sweating, skin discoloration, cutaneous vasculitis, pain and discomfort at the site of application; muscle pain, arthritis, weakness, joint pain, muscle spasm, back pain; urticaria, rash, itching, angioedema or an anaphylactoid reaction.

groups.title: Capsule (A97900ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment for damaged hair, for poor growth of the nails that is not caused by infection, and for hair loss.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Children aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day, after meals. The average duration of treatment is 3 to 6 months.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 12 years of age, or for hair loss caused by scarring, androgenetic hereditary alopecia or male-pattern baldness.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with a sulfonamide preparation.

If gastrointestinal discomfort (stomach pain, vomiting), sweating, tachycardia, itching, urticaria, headache, dizziness, flushing, or growth of hair on parts of the body other than the head occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Adjunctive treatment of damaged hair, poor nail growth not caused by infection, and hair loss

groups.title: Capsule (146602ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the improvement of symptoms related to venous insufficiency (a feeling of heaviness in the legs, pain and the like), as adjunctive treatment of disorders caused by capillary fragility, and for the treatment of signs related to haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day (with lunch and with dinner). If haemorrhoids recur or become worse, up to 4 to 6 capsules (1200 to 1800 mg) may be taken in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if you are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant.

Do not take it over a long period. If symptoms do not improve quickly, examination of the anus and a review of the treatment are needed.

If digestive disturbance occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (187502ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for its antacid action and for the improvement of symptoms in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and for constipation.
groups.usage: For gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid: take 1 to 2 capsules (0.5 to 1 g as magnesium oxide) in 1 day, divided into several doses. For constipation: take 4 capsules (2 g) in 1 day, divided into 1 to 2 doses. For the first dose, take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney impairment or diarrhoea.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart function, hypermagnesaemia, or if you are an older person (aged 65 years or older).

Because the adsorbent action of this medicine or the rise in the pH of the fluid in the digestive tract may affect the absorption and excretion of medicines taken with it, it should be given with care.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take tetracycline antibiotics. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a large amount of milk or with calcium preparations.

If dizziness on standing up, slowing of the pulse, strong drowsiness, clouding of consciousness, a feeling of suffocation, muscle weakness, dry mouth or vomiting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Symptoms of magnesium poisoning and, occasionally, diarrhoea may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Antacid action and symptom relief in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and constipation

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Capsule (303404ACE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis, impaired iron utilisation (anaemia due to lead poisoning, sideroachrestic anaemia, thalassaemia, porphyria cutanea tarda), anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency (megaloblastic anaemia due to vitamin B12 deficiency), anaemia due to bone marrow failure, chronic haemolytic anaemia, iron overload, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis, liver cirrhosis, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis, impaired heart or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney impairment, hypoproteinaemia, if you are being given an iron-containing preparation (an iron supplement, an MRI liver contrast agent and the like), if you have delayed gastric emptying, pyloric stenosis or a gastrointestinal diverticulum, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine, triamterene, iron preparations and diphosphonate salts, thyroxine, a cefdinir preparation, salicylic acid, phenylbutazone, oxyphenbutazone with iron preparations, a quinolone, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract or a preparation such as vitamin E. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: urticaria, itching, skin hypersensitivity on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, coma, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, tooth discoloration, stomach discomfort; occasionally raised AST and ALT; rarely raised ALP.

summaryTable.What it is for: Prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A50200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin E and vitamin B2 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, and in old age, and for the relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance, stiffness of the shoulder and neck at the menopause, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet, angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 8 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen or with an intravenous lipid preparation.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, loss of appetite or a feeling of fullness in the abdomen occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the amount gradually increases, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamin E and B2 and relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance, shoulder and neck stiffness at the menopause, numb and cold hands and feet, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis

groups.title: Eye Drops (D01200COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, for supplementing tears (dryness of the eye), for discomfort while wearing hard or soft contact lenses, and for blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 3 drops per dose, 3 to 6 times in 1 day. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container immediately.
groups.caution:
Consult a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain, if you have ever had an allergic reaction to an eye medicine (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, reddening and the like), or if you have glaucoma.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If blurring of the eyes does not improve with this medicine, stop using it and consult a pharmacist. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. To prevent contamination, do not share it with others. After opening, use it only once immediately and discard the remaining solution and the container at once. Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or the eyelashes, and do not use the solution if it is cloudy.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Eye fatigue, tear supplementation (dry eye), discomfort with contact lenses and blurred eyes

groups.title: Medicated Gum (A87801AMS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid to stopping smoking; it reduces the amount smoked and helps you to give up cigarettes.
groups.usage: For adults, the 2 mg gum is recommended for smokers of 20 or fewer cigarettes a day, and the 4 mg gum is recommended for heavy smokers of more than 20 cigarettes a day or when the 2 mg strength has not worked. Use it whenever there is an urge to smoke.
groups.caution:
It may stick to dental prostheses and dentures and, in rare cases, may damage them.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, unstable angina, worsening angina, myocardial infarction within the past 3 months, the late phase after an acute infarction, severe cardiac arrhythmia, systemic hypertension, peripheral vascular disease, acute stroke or cerebrovascular disease; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child or adolescent under 18 years of age; or if the user is a non-smoker or an occasional smoker.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have gastritis, gastric or duodenal ulcer, occlusive arterial disease, stable angina, heart failure, decompensated heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, vasospasm, uncontrolled high blood pressure, an arterial bypass graft or angioplasty; if you are an older person; if you have kidney failure, liver failure, diabetes, hyperthyroidism or phaeochromocytoma; if you are a smoker with dentures; or if you have had epilepsy or seizures.

Chewing it quickly may sometimes cause unpleasant symptoms, so chew it slowly. Chewing several pieces at the same time may cause serious symptoms of overdose, so do not chew several pieces at once.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, oestrogens, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (prazosin, labetalol and the like), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (isoprenaline, phenylephrine), propoxyphene, the diuretic furosemide, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, tacrine, clozapine, ropinirole, olanzapine, clomipramine or fluvoxamine.

If any of the following occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: headache, dizziness, sleep disturbance, anxiety, emotional instability, agitation, abnormal dreams, confusion, restlessness, difficulty concentrating, fatigue, migraine, spasm, leg cramps, seizures; changes in blood pressure, high blood pressure, palpitations, reversible atrial fibrillation, atrial arrhythmia; nausea, vomiting, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, indigestion, flatulence (abdominal distension), gastrointestinal disorders such as gastric ulcer, difficulty swallowing, thirst, abnormal bowel movements, constipation, diarrhoea, increased appetite; cold and influenza symptoms, cough, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, upper respiratory symptoms, bronchitis, difficulty breathing; allergy, skin eruption, herpes eruption, itching, urticaria, acne, erythema (red patches); distortion of taste, abnormal vision, irritation (pain) of the mouth and throat, pain of the jaw joint and muscles, gingivitis; dysmenorrhoea, muscle pain, joint pain, toothache, back pain, chest pain, pain, earache, facial flushing, local swelling, weight gain, thyroid dysfunction, pain of the lymph nodes, cystitis, increased sweating, hiccups or angioedema.

groups.title: Eye Drops (A54700COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, for supplementing tears (dryness of the eye), for discomfort while wearing hard or soft contact lenses, and for blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 3 drops per dose, 3 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to eye medicines, severe eye pain or glaucoma.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, or if a wearer of hard contact lenses has a lot of discharge such as eye mucus or the lenses become cloudy, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (241101ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for vitamin E deficiency, for impaired peripheral circulation, and for the relief of symptoms such as stiffness of the shoulder and neck at the menopause, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet, intermittent claudication (occasional limping) and frostbite.
groups.usage: Adults: take 50 IU to 1000 IU of vitamin E in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil, soybean or peanut, or if you are breast-feeding. Avoid taking high doses of this medicine during pregnancy.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; if you have had bronchial asthma, rash or urticaria; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; if the user is a child taking an iron preparation; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, vitamin A or vitamin K preparations, oral anticoagulants, the anti-obesity medicine orlistat, a mineral-oil laxative, an iron preparation or an intravenous lipid preparation.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, muscle weakness, fatigue, headache or blurred vision (with long-term use) occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the amount gradually increases, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
